decisions.summary: make set-down removes the clone's active-task mark once the set-down row is written, when the mark names the set-down feature, and says so in its reply; the next task-start writes it again
decisions.why: Fixes a defect in the sense of constitution XIV (a tool refusing valid work: a set-down feature's stale mark held every push touching its specs and refused T06's landing). It narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: A refused set-down, another feature's mark, or a mark that cannot be read or names no feature is left as it stands and fails nothing
decisions.why: None of these cases is the defect. Clearing another feature's mark, or clearing the mark after a refused set-down, would be wrong. Leaving an unreadable mark as it is does not take back any part of the stated goal: a set-down feature no longer holds pushes through its own mark.

decisions.summary: Tagged [perf] in FR-013's sense (it makes the landings faster), not filed with PERF=1 because it touches no engine stage's counted operations or time
decisions.why: FR-013 defines performance work to include a task that makes the landings faster. A stale mark cost a refused landing and reverted ticks. The PERF=1 distinction follows FR-013's two routes as written.

decisions.summary: Red-first test, 100% line coverage of the task crate, the clear deleted to show the test turns red, a scratch-repo replay of the incident, and the usual green exits

decisions.why: Nothing is narrowed or left: the defect T30 was filed for is fixed, only in a different task, because T15's plan review ruled leaving it NOT LEGITIMATE. Moving where a fix lands does not shrink what was asked; 'Found and left? none'.

decisions.summary: Done is T15 ticked with the fix; the red exit records what failed, sets the task down, and routes any cannot-be-done claim through make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: A completion condition and a standard failure route; it carves out no case and defers no defect.

decisions.summary: Kept as a [perf] task under FR-013, folded into T15.
decisions.why: Classification under FR-013's own definition (work that makes the checks/gate/builders' loop faster or correct); it narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: Feature 204's D5 ('every python3 -c is a write') narrowed: a -c program a denylist of known writers judges read-only (read-mode opens only, no substitution/expansion, no relative or locally-answerable import) is marked how=read and is no write, unless the command also runs Python from stdin.
decisions.why: Not a narrowing of feature 451's request or spec (the D5/D6 in spec-cited.md are 451's own decisions; 204's D5 is known only as the plan quotes it). Ruled anyway. rulings.md is empty, so the session's own ruling carries no weight; the ground is the constitution's defect definition: a guard that refuses or rewrites a read refuses good work. D5's premise ('its cost is now zero') is measured false where no clone resolves (80 corpus rows refused clone-unresolved, 79 rewritten, replay 2026-11-20). D5's purpose (no false allow) is kept by the conservative conditions and the stdin rule (parse#72, window#61 refused as before). The denylist ends in '...', so its full reach is not visible in the bundle; not a finding.

decisions.summary: A -c read stays a write when any segment of the same command runs Python from stdin (python3 -, heredoc, < file, | python3).
decisions.why: Keeps T31 from turning measured heredoc writers (parse#72, window#61) from refused into allowed; it adds no allowance.

decisions.summary: Three real heredoc reads (main-tree#147, window#339, window#361) stay refused or rewritten, as before T31, as the stdin rule's cost; recorded under Found and left and homed in T42, which retires the stdin rule once stdin bodies are judged, landing before T22.
decisions.why: The previous round's BLOCKED asked for exactly this: the known defect now has a home. Found and left names the three rows, how they were found (the replays' rows that moved back against the stage-1 build, each hand-read), why T31 does not fix them (no stdin reader exists, and lifting the rule without one lets parse#72's and window#61's writes through - trading a refused read for an allowed write), and a filed task (T42) that retires the rule once stdin bodies are judged, ordered before T22. T31 does not worsen these rows (they were refused or rewritten before it). Limit: T42's own task line (said in the dispatch to commit to retiring the rule, red first on these three rows) is not in the bundle; the block's own words 'which retires the rule once stdin bodies are judged' are what was read.

decisions.summary: Four rows that also run a script (main-tree#103 scratch script; window#60, #62, #308 the mirror's own test suites and hooks), refused or moved before only by the -c write, now run as typed without being shown to write nothing.
decisions.why: T31 changes nothing about how a script run is judged: the same commands without the -c read are allowed today, so their earlier refusal was a side effect of the defect fixed (a read misjudged as a write). The hand-read found no writer in any of the four, unlike parse#72/window#61, so no defect is shown, and keeping a misjudged read refused to cover an unjudged segment would keep the defect. Item 1's 'every write is still moved or refused as before' slightly overstates this for these rows; item 4 discloses it.

decisions.summary: Judging Python heredoc/stdin bodies for writes (301 corpus rows main-tree allows before and after) deferred to T42, landing before T22.
decisions.why: A defect left (writes in the mirror passed), but it predates T31 and T31 does not worsen it (301 allowed before and after, measured 2026-11-20). It is outside the -c scope, needs a new reader with its own replay, is recorded under Found and left with its reason, and is homed in a filed task (T42) with an ordering (before T22).

decisions.why: The same defect (a read refused) in the second guard that reads a walk's targets; red first (gmred.log).

decisions.why: Records the fix's measured outcome; no new behavior.

decisions.summary: Fix the 6 tests that the 79-variable sweep showed moving (RECORD_CHECKS_DIR, L7R_GUARD_TREE, SET_DOWN_ROOT, L7R_PERMIT_NOW x2, L7R_DISPATCHER), and stop the event-log tests writing fixture logs into an exported L7R_EVENTS_DIR.
decisions.why: Known defects of the same kind, fixed in the task that found them (fix as we go). The stray event-log writes matter directly to this feature, because they corrupt the logs that where-time and the GM's retrospective read.

decisions.summary: Convert the 7 tests that set the process environment to set the test thread's own map, converting their reads with them.
decisions.why: Same mechanism, same task. It widens no behavior beyond the guard crate's tests.

decisions.summary: Leave log::quiet's GUARD_LOG_DIR set once for the whole process (T009), and leave the binary's main.rs and bench.rs reading the real environment.
decisions.why: Neither is a wrong outcome. GUARD_LOG_DIR is set once on purpose, to keep test logs out of real ones. main.rs and bench.rs are not tests and must read the real environment. The GM's request asks for no rule against process-environment mutation; that wording is the task line's own. Leaving a difference that works is not a narrowing (constitution XIV).

decisions.summary: Leave MEASURE_STATE_DIR (a test created the directory empty and wrote nothing into it) and the reads that the sweep showed moving no test, as not defects.
decisions.why: Measured to produce no wrong outcome (ls of the exported directory; per-var.tsv). Under constitution XIV these are not defects, and nothing the GM asked is left undone.

decisions.summary: The gate crates' tests reading the real environment through the guard (49 tests in 7 crates red with L7R_FEATURE_DIRECTORY and L7R_EVENTS_DIR exported) are not fixed in T32. They are filed as T38, ordered to land before T22, with the reason stated: the guard's test map is cfg(test) of the guard alone, so the fix is a reader threaded to 17 call sites in 7 crates, each owing its own test, lint and cover.
decisions.why: The defect is not dropped or left unfixed in the feature. It is scheduled as its own task in the same feature, with a stated reason and an ordering, which is what FR-009 requires of a deferral. T32's filed scope is the guard crate's own tests, so moving work outside that crate into a separate task narrows nothing the GM asked for. This would be a finding only if T38 were not performance-tagged or never landed, and this block cannot show either.

decisions.summary: no_poll_hooks, named by T14's run, is not fixed: it failed in none of 4 exported runs and none of the sweep's 91, and it is named in the report.
decisions.why: No wrong outcome was reproduced, so no known defect is left. Naming it in the report is the honest handling.

decisions.summary: T32 is classed as performance work ([perf], FR-013): a builder's make rust-test on the guard is green whatever the session exports.
decisions.why: FR-013 counts 'the builders' loop faster' as performance work. A false red that costs a builder a round falls inside that definition and inside the GM's 2026-11-20 'prioritize performance improvements'.

decisions.summary: Order: after T24 (its seam is reused), independent of T20. Exits: crate-scoped lint and cover, make quick, make static once, make hooks-test; on red, the task is set down and any claim that it cannot be done goes through make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: The ordering and exits are consistent with FR-007 (make static once, crate-scoped checks while iterating). Nothing requested is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Part 1: guard_write reads an inline interpreter body (Python literals resolved where the shell stands, -c/heredoc bodies as commands, Perl/Ruby/Node by the same literal reading, a for loop's variable per word), with a literal only read, a subprocess argv and a dict value exempt.
decisions.why: Closes the observed T14 hole (a heredoc rewrite of a guard source). The three exemptions each answer a measured false refusal of correct work (replay round 1: window#56, #299, #312, #267), and no real write in the 1,134 rows passes through them. That is a precision choice inside the task, not a narrowing of what was asked.

decisions.summary: A shell or interpreter write of a guard file stays refused under a live guard-edit permit, as sed -i is at HEAD; the permit is for the Edit tool.
decisions.why: This keeps HEAD's rule for sed -i and extends it to the new forms. It narrows nothing, because the compliant route (the Edit tool under the permit) remains, and the block message names it.

decisions.summary: A bare rustfmt is refused as bare-rustfmt, and the message names make format FILE= / CRATE=.
decisions.why: Closes the observed T34 hole, with the compliant command named.

decisions.summary: shell_write refuses a write that the walk or a Python literal places in the gated tree while its gate runs. Only a literal that resolves to a path where the shell stands counts, and an unresolvable path fails open, as the walk does.
decisions.why: Closes the observed T34 hole (git apply / cp under a running land). Failing open on an unresolvable path is the gate's existing rule, not a new carve-out, and the 18 outside-the-tree rows it lets through were measured as correct work.

decisions.summary: A literal handed to a function of the program's own is counted where the shell stands (fail-closed). window#72, a correct write into another clone that HEAD allowed, is now refused under a running gate. Left unfixed, filed as T49, lands before T22.
decisions.why: This is the only item T33 leaves that makes HEAD worse. By the block's own account window#72 is a correct write that moves allowed->refused, a check refusing good work, which is a defect by constitution XIV. It contradicts the section's goal 1 ('nothing correct is refused by the new reading') and its constraint 2 (XIII, no known regressions). The reason given, that placing the literal needs the function's body and no reader of interp does, is a cost argument. It meets none of the criteria: nothing is physically impossible, the request implies no such case, and fixing it would not defeat the request's purpose. The block also stretches one justification over two unlike guards. It cites make-only's fail-closed count for this literal, while it states gate-write's own rule as failing open on a path it cannot place. The available escape (GATE_WRITE_OK, or waiting for the gate) does not make a false refusal correct, and a feature whose purpose is efficiency is worse off for a guard that stops correct work. FR-009's form (why, id, order) is met, but the form is not legitimacy. To clear it, window#72 is not refused by what lands in T33, or the section gives a reason that meets one of the three criteria.

decisions.summary: chmod's mode and chown's owner are no longer read as files (shared/tree.rs tool_paths).
decisions.why: Fixes HEAD's own false refusals that the replay found (refusals#132, window#256), as FIX AS WE GO requires.

decisions.summary: git_output reads the writing options of the read-only subcommands (--output, archive -o, format-patch, bundle create, bugreport, diagnose). stash list/show are reads, and the gate's commit-or-add rule reads git's subcommand, not the word anywhere in the segment.
decisions.why: Closes the observed T44 hole (git diff --output read as a read). The stash and commit-or-add changes fix false refusals the replay measured (parse#148, #171, #173, #229, refusals#88, window#279), plus one the new check would otherwise have introduced.

decisions.summary: The addition reading twelve git subcommands outside GIT_WRITES as writes was built, measured and dropped, and filed as a measure-first task T50, lands before T22.
decisions.why: The observed hole (git diff --output) is fixed. What is left is inherited from HEAD, and no wrong outcome is recorded for it: the replay of 1,134 rows caught no real write with the addition, and its only moves were its own false refusals. Under the defect definition nothing defective is left, so the drop does not narrow the request. The dispatch's and the session's rulings are not the GM's and carry no weight here; this is judged on the end state alone.

decisions.summary: A program run from a file (python3 script.py) is not read. One real case was found (window#215 rewriting a clone's Makefile), plus seven clone writes the gate would see. Filed as T51, lands before T22.
decisions.why: I read this as a fifth form outside T33's four observed holes, not as part of hole 1. Hole 1's mechanism reads a body handed inline to the interpreter, and a script file is a separate artifact needing a reader no guard has. HEAD has the same gap (T33 does not worsen it). It was found by a census the section records with its method, and it is filed with an id and an order under FR-009. If hole 1 were read as covering every interpreter write, this would be a narrowing whose reason (cost, plus the need for its own replay) meets no criterion. I chose the narrower reading of the task's observed forms.

decisions.summary: DEPTH 3 for nested bodies, stated as a convention past any shape in the corpora.
decisions.why: Measured as covering every row; it narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: After T14 and T15, lands with T07, one landing. Exits include make static once, plus rust-test, lint, format, cover, quick and hooks-test.
decisions.why: Sequencing and exits consistent with FR-007 (make static once) and the guard rules.

decisions.summary: Performance work? no.
decisions.why: A classification. Whether T33 may start while a performance task is open is FR-013's guard's call on task state that the bundle does not carry; it is not a decision of this section.

decisions.summary: Add `make format FILE=<path...>` and `make format CRATE=<dir>`, which format only what they name; bare `make format` is unchanged.
decisions.why: A [perf] task on the builders' loop under FR-013, which comes from the GM's 2026-11-20 'can we in general priotitize performance improvements going forward?'. It is also the same kind of fix as approved improvement 2 (a crate-scoped step while iterating instead of a whole-tree one). Nothing asked for is narrowed, since the whole-tree form stays as it was.

decisions.summary: The one-file path feeds the file to the toolchain's rustfmt on standard input, run from the file's directory (so rustfmt.toml is found), with --edition taken from the owning crate's Cargo.toml (2015 where it names none), and writes the file only where rustfmt passed and changed it.
decisions.why: This is how the requested behavior gets done. Standard input was chosen on a dated scratch measurement showing that a path argument rewrites the file's `mod` children, which would break 'formats only what it names'. The plan's step 9 records that `--check --crate` was clean after FILE= runs, so the output matches cargo fmt.

decisions.summary: A Cargo.toml edition that is not a literal (for example an inherited one) is refused on the FILE= path.
decisions.why: This refuses an input it cannot read rather than guessing an edition and formatting wrongly. CRATE= and bare `make format` still cover such a crate. It does not narrow anything the request or spec asks for.

decisions.summary: FILE=/CRATE= format takes no run lock and never waits on another run's tests, because it builds nothing.
decisions.why: This serves the performance purpose (FR-013, the builders' loop) and does not narrow any requirement.

decisions.summary: FILE= given together with CRATE= is refused (exit 2), and the `format` failure's tip names CRATE= and FILE= instead of bare `make format`.
decisions.why: Usage guarding, and pointing builders at the scoped forms, serve the task's own purpose (not rewriting another builder's in-progress files). Nothing is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Found and left (a): the make-only guard does not refuse a bare `rustfmt`. Deferred to T33 (held writes through a route the guard does not read), which lands before T22.
decisions.why: This is a narrowing because the block calls it a defect (a check that lets bad work through), and approved improvement 4 makes fixing in the task the default for briefs. FR-009, judged against its index line only since the bundle carries nothing more, requires a deferral to state why the defect is not fixed here, and this one does. The guard is rust/guard, where T31's builder has work in progress. Fixing it inside T34 means editing, linting and covering a crate that holds another builder's half-done files, which is the clobbering of in-progress work that T34 exists to stop, and T34's green exit cannot be met honestly over that crate now. So a literal fix-in-task would defeat the task's purpose. The defect is not left: it is filed in this feature as T33, with an order (before T22), and T33's class (writes by a route the guard does not read) matches it exactly.

decisions.summary: Found and left (b): the make-only guard's block message advertises bare `make format`, which rewrites every crate. Deferred with (a), 'Filed as T33'.
decisions.why: Ruled separately from (a), because a message's wording is not a 'route the guard does not read' and T33's class argument does not reach it. Only the location argument carries it. That argument is enough: the message text lives in rust/guard, where T31's builder works now, so the same purpose-level and exit-level reasons as (a) apply. The interim harm is reduced inside T34 itself, since `make format`'s own failure tip and `make help` now name FILE= and CRATE=. The block's 'Filed as T33' covers its whole bullet, both the guard gap and the message, so T33 owes the message fix as well as the refusal. A T33 that fixes only the refusal would leave (b) unfixed.

decisions.summary: Add `make format FILE=<path...>` and `make format CRATE=<dir>`, which format only what they name; bare `make format` is unchanged.
decisions.why: A [perf] task on the builders' loop under FR-013, which comes from the GM's 2026-11-20 'can we in general priotitize performance improvements going forward?'. It is also the same kind of fix as approved improvement 2 (a crate-scoped step while iterating instead of a whole-tree one). Nothing asked for is narrowed, since the whole-tree form stays as it was.

decisions.summary: The one-file path feeds the file to the toolchain's rustfmt on standard input, run from the file's directory (so rustfmt.toml is found), with --edition taken from the owning crate's Cargo.toml (2015 where it names none), and writes the file only where rustfmt passed and changed it.
decisions.why: This is how the requested behavior gets done. Standard input was chosen on a dated scratch measurement showing that a path argument rewrites the file's `mod` children, which would break 'formats only what it names'. The plan's step 9 records that `--check --crate` was clean after FILE= runs, so the output matches cargo fmt.

decisions.summary: A Cargo.toml edition that is not a literal (for example an inherited one) is refused on the FILE= path.
decisions.why: This refuses an input it cannot read rather than guessing an edition and formatting wrongly. CRATE= and bare `make format` still cover such a crate. It does not narrow anything the request or spec asks for.

decisions.summary: FILE=/CRATE= format takes no run lock and never waits on another run's tests, because it builds nothing.
decisions.why: This serves the performance purpose (FR-013, the builders' loop) and does not narrow any requirement.

decisions.summary: FILE= given together with CRATE= is refused (exit 2), and the `format` failure's tip names CRATE= and FILE= instead of bare `make format`.
decisions.why: Usage guarding, and pointing builders at the scoped forms, serve the task's own purpose (not rewriting another builder's in-progress files). Nothing is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Found and left (a): the make-only guard does not refuse a bare `rustfmt`. Deferred to T33 (held writes through a route the guard does not read), which lands before T22.
decisions.why: This is a narrowing because the block calls it a defect (a check that lets bad work through), and approved improvement 4 makes fixing in the task the default for briefs. FR-009, judged against its index line only since the bundle carries nothing more, requires a deferral to state why the defect is not fixed here, and this one does. The guard is rust/guard, where T31's builder has work in progress. Fixing it inside T34 means editing, linting and covering a crate that holds another builder's half-done files, which is the clobbering of in-progress work that T34 exists to stop, and T34's green exit cannot be met honestly over that crate now. So a literal fix-in-task would defeat the task's purpose. The defect is not left: it is filed in this feature as T33, with an order (before T22), and T33's class (writes by a route the guard does not read) matches it exactly.

decisions.summary: Found and left (b): the make-only guard's block message advertises bare `make format`, which rewrites every crate. Deferred with (a), 'Filed as T33'.
decisions.why: Ruled separately from (a), because a message's wording is not a 'route the guard does not read' and T33's class argument does not reach it. Only the location argument carries it. That argument is enough: the message text lives in rust/guard, where T31's builder works now, so the same purpose-level and exit-level reasons as (a) apply. The interim harm is reduced inside T34 itself, since `make format`'s own failure tip and `make help` now name FILE= and CRATE=. The block's 'Filed as T33' covers its whole bullet, both the guard gap and the message, so T33 owes the message fix as well as the refusal. A T33 that fixes only the refusal would leave (b) unfixed.
